The little guide to budgeting.

A budget is a plan for the money you have. It helps you decide what needs paying, what you want to keep for later, and what you can enjoy now. You can change the plan when life changes.

Start with one month.

You don’t need perfect numbers, a fixed salary, or a list of every purchase. A few useful categories and a quick check-in are enough to begin.

01 · Get started

Make your first split

  1. Enter the income you have for this month. If more comes in later, update the amount.
  2. List your important costs first. Think feeding, rent, transport, bills, data, debt payments, and anything your household relies on.
  3. Choose your groups. Rename the starter categories or add more in Edit split. Tap Need category ideas? if you want prompts.
  4. Give the groups percentages that add to 100%. A new group begins at 0%; move some percentage from another group to fund it. The app turns your percentages into amounts. No universal split fits everyone, so use numbers you can live with.
Example: if ₦100,000 comes in and feeding gets 25%, your feeding plan is ₦25,000. The percentage is a starting decision, not a rule.
02 · When income changes

Plan for the month you have

If your income changes, start with a cautious amount that covers the costs you cannot skip. When more money arrives, update the month’s income and choose where the extra goes. For unusual months, Edit split → This month lets you change percentages without rewriting your usual plan.

Look ahead for school fees, yearly bills, trips, and other costs that are easy to forget. You can set money aside a little at a time in a category you name for that purpose.

03 · Keep going

A check-in takes a minute

Once a week, or whenever you remember, tap Check in. Enter the total spent or set aside so far this month in each category. For example, if you spent ₦4,000 on transport and then ₦2,000 more, enter ₦6,000. The app shows how much remains against the plan.

Only fill in the categories you know. If a category goes over, that’s information for the next decision, not a failure. You can adjust this month’s percentages if your needs change.

04 · Helpful habits

Make it easy to return

  • Pick a tiny routine. A Sunday check-in or a check-in each time income arrives is plenty.
  • Keep a buffer if you can. Emergency savings are for unexpected costs, even small ones. Start with an amount that fits your situation.
  • Name things clearly. “Feeding” and “Transport” are easier to revisit than a vague “Other.” Savings is money you set aside; investing is a different goal with possible losses, so learn about a choice before committing money to it.
  • Expect edits. A useful budget bends when prices or priorities change.
05 · Your data

Keep your budget with you

Little Ledger saves entries in this browser on this device. Add a PIN from the top of the budget to lock and encrypt them here. Your phone passcode can also help protect access to your phone, but it does not replace the app PIN. Save a backup in Edit split before changing phones or browsers. A PIN protected backup needs that same PIN to restore, and a lost PIN cannot be recovered.
